title: Generic-point full faithfulness for finite etale covers of a normal integral scheme
statement: Let B be an integral scheme with integrally closed local rings [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. For finite etale πX:X → B and πY:Y → B, let Xη and Yη be any cartesian restrictions to Spec K(B), with projections πXη, πYη and comparison maps ψX, ψY [def-pc-fibre-product]. Every morphism fη:Xη → Yη satisfying fη;πYη=πXη admits a unique f:X → Y such that f;πY=πX and ψX;f=fη;ψY. The covers may be empty or disconnected. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0BQM, full faithfulness in the proof; Tag 0BQL, normalization of finite etale covers

proof.text: Let j:Spec K(B) → B. The existing source-library theorem Scheme.isIso_fromNormalization_restrict, recorded at lem-sc-normalization-over-normal-locus, is stated for every integral scheme, without the blueprint node's finite-type restriction. Apply it to the top open and hB, and remove the two top-open inclusions to obtain IsIso j.fromNormalization. This uses its already proved general Lean interface; no finite-type or Noetherian assumption is needed.

Let P=Spec K(B) ×_B X, k:P → X, and let e:Xη ≅ P be the pullback isomorphism from hX.flip. Since πX is etale, it is smooth. Relative normalization commutes with smooth base change: k.fromNormalization is the composite of the normalizationPullback comparison with the pullback of j.fromNormalization. Both factors are isomorphisms, so k.fromNormalization is an isomorphism.

Let T=Y ×_B X and q:T → X be its second projection, which is finite because πY is finite. The map a=e.inv;fη;ψY satisfies a;πY=k;πX by hfη and the two cartesian-square equations. The pullback lift b=(a,k):P → T therefore satisfies b;q=k. Normalization's universal property gives d:k.normalization → T with toNormalization;d=b and d;q=fromNormalization. Set s=inv(fromNormalization);d. Then s;q=id_X and ψX;s=e.hom;b. Thus f=s;fst:T → Y (with domain X after s) lies over B and satisfies ψX;f=fη;ψY.

For another such g, form the section t=(g,id_X):X → T. The maps fromNormalization;t and fromNormalization;s have the same composite with q and the same restriction along toNormalization. The latter equality is checked after the pullback isomorphism e and then by the two projections of T, using the given generic compatibility for g. Apply normalization.hom_ext and cancel the isomorphism fromNormalization to obtain t=s. Composing with fst gives g=f. This proves the original unique-existence statement, including empty and disconnected covers.
